rv.q: This is a magnificent revival and, along with 1536 and James Graham’s incoming The Standard of Living, evidence perhaps of the possible resurgence of straight plays in the West End.

Certainly the last major London revival – a brooding, rap-battling affair directed by Jamie Lloyd – was a case in point. James McAvoy starred as Cyrano, the brilliant wordsmith with an obtrusively big schnozz.
I’ve rarely seen anything as heartbreaking.
Lester's Cyrano is magnificent, his sharp wit barely covering a long, deep anger at his treatment by society.
The production is playful and funny with poignant, moving moments interspersed with sharp wit.
A dazzling, ultimately moving show
A beautiful, romantic production that says more than the words alone ever could.
Fiercely funny and intensely romantic, Cyrano lives by his words and his sword.
I am so pleased that I was able to see this particular rendering.
He is tremendous, the thrilling centre of a raucous yet touching production.
The poetic rhythm of the play is simply exquisite, seamlessly flowing from verse to prose.
The team have doubled down on the heartbreak of politesse in the face of a cautiously held but unrequited love, creating perhaps one of the most moving endings to a production of Cyrano ever staged.
It’s a risky device – handled wrongly it could have been sentimental – but here it adds a genuine poignancy.
What Simon Evans and Debris Stevenson have created here is nothing short of spectacular, with Adrian Lester’s leading turn delivering a performance for the ages.
The sword fighting sequences designed by Bethan Clark took my breath away: it would be worth seeing the production just for these.
This is going to become a Cyrano I recall with pleasure.
This is a true triumph and London is so lucky to receive it for the summer.
Transferred to the West End from its stellar run at Stratford, this production is the RSC at its best.
Original, moving and technically exceptional, it's one of the finest revivals currently in the West End.
It’s funny, inventive, technically slick, and emotionally overwhelming, a production that invites audiences to laugh loudly before quietly breaking their hearts.

cn.t: The RSC's exuberant Cyrano earns rapturous reviews, with Adrian Lester delivering a magnificent performance. Critics praise the witty, contemporary adaptation that honors Rostand's romanticism while feeling fresh and emotionally resonant.
